topic: Choosing a mattress: what actually matters

slides.headline: Mattress shopping? What actually matters
slides.sub: Firm or soft? The answer is more personal than the ads suggest.

slides.title: Medium-firm is a starting point
slides.body: Research suggests a medium-firm mattress suits many people with back pain better than a very firm one. It's a starting point rather than a rule. How you feel when you wake up matters most.

slides.title: Match it to how you sleep
slides.body: Side sleepers often like a bit more give at the shoulder and hip. Back and stomach sleepers usually prefer a little more support. Couples may need a compromise, or a split-firmness option.

slides.title: Test it properly
slides.body: Lie on it for 10 to 15 minutes in your usual sleeping position, not 30 seconds in the showroom. If a trial period is offered, check the conditions carefully before you commit.

slides.title: The mattress isn't everything
slides.body: Pillow height, room temperature, stress and how active you were that day all affect morning stiffness. On a hot Sydney summer night, a cooler room can matter as much as new foam.

slides.title: When to get it checked
slides.body: Back pain that's worse at night whatever position you're in, pain with fever or unexplained weight loss, or numbness or weakness in the legs deserve an assessment, not another mattress.

slides.headline: Waking up stiff every morning?
slides.body: Our chiropractors at Hybrid Physiotherapy look at your back, sleep setup and daily load, then combine hands-on care with exercise. Book online, link in bio.

caption:
Thinking about a new mattress? Ignore the marketing for a minute.

Research suggests medium-firm suits many people with back pain better than very firm, but comfort is personal. Side sleepers often want more give at the hips and shoulders, while back sleepers usually like more support.

Test it for 10 to 15 minutes in your normal sleep position, and remember the mattress is only one piece. Pillow height, a cooler room, stress and daily activity all play a part in how your back feels at 7am.

Night pain that doesn't change with position, or pain with fever, weight loss or leg numbness, deserves an assessment.
